RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 30

An all-male panel is not evidence of discrimination on its own — it's a context factor, not a finding. Panels in many ministries skew male simply because senior grades do. On its own it proves nothing about how they scored you.

Your stronger ground is procedural: a two-week-old unanswered request for written reasons, and a successful candidate who appears less qualified on paper (no law degree, fewer civil service years) selected on a vaguely worded criterion — "experience of leading international projects" — that may not have been in the published person specification.

So: chase the written reasons formally, in writing, with a deadline. Mention panel composition only as supporting context if the reasons turn out to be thin or shifting.
